items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: every summer from then on until I was about 18, my father would let me go down to Houston and play with Sid Isles.

ctx.x: I'm L.D. Harris. My real name is Lawrence Douglas Harris. I was born and raised in Brenham, Texas. That's about 165 miles from here. It's on H and T.C. between Austin and Houston, Texas. And I started out playing music between the ages of 13 and 14, started studying music. They organized a boys band there. I had a fellow who had been in the service by the name of Gus Allen. Everybody called him Uncle Beansy. He's quite a musician. And my father and several other fathers there in the city thought it would be a…
John Johnson. You want to go there one time?

items.title: Lawrence Douglas Harris Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: I played for her. And that little boy out of Houston... my name was Skinny, he couldn't read but he could play the best piano player ever in my life.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Well when I left there I left there with Ida Cox.

Incidentally I see where she gotta write up where she stuff Yeah, she cut out and cut some records again. I'd like to hear that. I played for her. And that little boy out of Houston, I don't know if you remember him, dog, my name was Skinny, he couldn't read but he could play the best piano player ever in my life. He was really terrific.

Well it seemed in those days, I'll say from the early 20s to the first to the 30s, most of the piano players, they didn't read. You take in New Orleans, Paul, there were a number of piano players while they couldn't read but played so terrific piano.
